core.title: Name job steps with the canonical step vocabulary, by reference to the step-vocabulary convention
core.given: Job steps are being named, or this rule's own reference to the step vocabulary is being edited
core.when: you assign a label to a job step or change how this rule points at the canonical steps
core.then: Label every job step with one of the canonical steps owned by the step-vocabulary convention (steps.convention: Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude), taking the vocabulary by reference to that owner.
prefer: Use the exact canonical step names owned by steps.convention: Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude
In this rule's own text, point at steps.convention by reference for what the steps are and mean
avoid: Inventing synonyms or project-specific step names in place of the canonical steps

Re-enumerating or redefining the steps inside this rule's own text (e.g. adding its own list of step meanings, extra steps, or changed definitions); copying the step owner's content into this rule is drift
core.why: steps.convention owns the step vocabulary, so one shared set of step names keeps job steps consistent; this rule references that owner instead of copying or redefining it, because copies drift. Using a step name as a label is referencing; restating what the steps are is copying.
evidence: Every job step label is one of Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude
This rule's own text points at steps.convention and contains no own enumeration or redefinition of the steps
verification: Label check: every job step label, in any artifact, by any actor, in any phase, must be one of the canonical steps owned by the step-vocabulary convention; any other job step label is a finding.

Reference-not-restate check, scoped to this rule's own text only: the rule points at the step-vocabulary convention by reference and does not re-enumerate or redefine the steps; an edit to this rule that adds or changes step definitions or a standalone step list is a finding.

The checks do not cover text that uses step words (e.g. 'define', 'execute') as ordinary verbs without naming job steps, and never apply to the step-vocabulary convention itself, which owns and may define the vocabulary.

Whether text names job steps, and whether a label or an edit is non-canonical, is content judgement (llm_judged) unless the realization provides a step-term detector; the rule-edit trigger needs an observer that maps the edited artifact to this rule id (needs_new_observer). The core imposes no particular detector.

neutralityNotes: This convention is inherently stack-neutral: it governs planning vocabulary and the rule's own text, never a stack construct, so the core needs no profile data (profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty) and no obligation had to be dropped or added. Two kinds of concrete content were deliberately kept in the core rather than moved to the profile or bunOnly: (1) the sibling convention id 'steps.convention', which is an ATDD-family identifier (the whole obligation is 'by reference to that owner'), not a stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path; and (2) the nine canonical step names, which are method-level planning vocabulary owned by that convention; if a stack's steps owner enumerated a different set, the operative obligation is the by-reference clause, exactly as in the Bun rule. 'This protocol' in bun.json denotes the convention itself and is rendered as 'this rule'. The activation facts' prose notes (observability commentary only) are dropped by the neutral fact schema; their content is preserved in core verification[3]. The verifier term ids (canonical_steps, reference_not_restate) and the audit/trace/additions provenance blocks remain with the ATDD-Bun sidecar.
